_doc: Parallel-worlds demonstrator (design §5). See ../_worlds.py and composr/worlds.json for the model. This is a PREFERENCE dissent (vs composr's CONSTRAINT dissent) — worlds come in flavors. NOTE: the spec sketched a `kanagawa-fans` colour-theme world, but this corpus's verdict-of-verdict chain is the backspace-at-empty-prompt one, so the dissent world is grounded there instead (same flavor: a UX preference that rejects the upstream revert).

main.assumption: least-surprise — the upstream revert stands; backspace is a no-op at an empty prompt

shell-muscle-memory.assumption: users expect shell-style backspace-aborts-empty-prompt (muscle memory) over least-surprise

reduction_fixtures.query: What does Backspace do on an empty command prompt in helix?

expected_by_world.main: No-op (only deletes; never aborts) — verdict2 reverted the abort change, reinstating the original behaviour.
expected_by_world.shell-muscle-memory: Aborts the prompt — verdict1 stands because the revert (verdict2) is suppressed under the muscle-memory assumption.

reduction_fixtures.status: DEMONSTRATED 2026-08-03: eval-worlds --llm passed this fixture in both worlds (reducer claude:sonnet via the pluggable chat-provider seam; blind letter-labeled LLM-judge grading — ollama embeddings unavailable that run; deterministic reachability in CI). Also exercises non-monotonic, frontier-relative defeat: on `main` verdict2 defeats verdict1, which REINSTATES the original; the dissent world keeps verdict1 live.
